Darboux Wronskian solutions of Ito typed coupled KdV equation with exact solitonic solutions and conserved densities

Journal: Nuclear Physics B
Irfan Mahmood Email: mahirfan@yhaoo.com Affiliation: Department of Mathematics, , Colllege of Science, Shanghai University, Shanghai, 200444, P.R.China Affiliation: Centre for High Energy Physics, University of the Punjab, Lahore, 54590, Punjab, Pakistan    Hira Sohail Email: hirasohail02@outlook.com Affiliation: Centre for High Energy Physics, University of the Punjab, Lahore, 54590, Punjab, Pakistan    and Allah Ditta Email: mradshahid01@gmail.com Affiliation: Department of Mathematics, , Colllege of Science, Shanghai University, Shanghai, 200444, P.R.China
Abstract

In this article, we derive the Darboux solutions of Ito type coupled KdV equation in Darboux framework which is associated with Hirota Satsuma systems. Then we generalise NN-fold Darboux transformations in terms of Wronskians. We also derive the exact multi-solitonic solutions for the coupled field variables of that system in the background of zero seed solutions. The last section encloses the derivation of continuity equation with several conserved densities through its Riccati equation.

Keywords:
Ito type coupled KdV equation , Darboux transformation, Wronskians, Solitons

1 Introduction

The nonlinear solitonic equations have got considerable attentions in theory of integrable systems because of their wide applications in various domains of physics and applied mathematics. One of the very interesting and earliest solitonic equations is KdV equation that plays a crucial role in the study of hydrodynamics to describe the geometrical properties of wave propagations in shallow water [1] and has also been acknowledged as integrable model in the analysis of electron plasma waves phenomenon associated with cylindrical plasma system [2]. The study of solitonic solutions of nonlinear evolution equations attained substantial importance in modern theory of integrable systems in exploring algebraic and geometrical profiles with their physical aspects, for example in context of Bose-Einstein condensate different types of solitons such as bright solitons [3, 4] dark solitons [4], vortex solitons [5] and gap solitons [6] have been found while studying matter wave solitons. In this article we construct the solitonic solutions of Ito type coupled KdV equation wave equation

{ut=ux​x​x+6​u​ux+qxvt=2​(u​v)x\left\{\begin{array}[]{lr}u_{t}=u_{xxx}+6uu_{x}+q_{x}\\ v_{t}=2(uv)_{x}\end{array}\right. (1)

which also called Integrable coupled nonlinear wave. The above coupled nonlinear wave (CNW) equation (1) with q=v2q=v^{2} can be obtained as the parametric reduction of famous Ito system [7] has been applied as integrable model in various domains of physics and fluid mechanics. Recently, its integro-differential analogue [8] with mixed dark-bright solitonic solutions have been investigated. Moreover, that coupled nonlinear wave equation has earned much importance in theory of integrable systems as it involves the KdV structure and reduces to the ordinary KdV equation by setting the coupling variables vv as v=0v=0. Here, we apply Darboux transformation to investigate its solitonic solutions. That Darboux approach [9, 10, 11] has been acknowledged as one of the efficient tools in theory of integrable systems to calculate the exact solutions of these systems with their algebraic and geometrical properties. In literature number of successful implementations of this transformation have been shown as an efficient integrable tool which enhance its significance from physical point of views. Among these number of remarkable applications of DT few of them are mentioned here as applied in the analysis of electrodynamical features [12] in case of quantum cavity problems and also to investigate the geometrical properties of graphene [13] with exact solitonic solutions. Moreover, that method has also been applied fruitfully to construct the quasideterminant solutions of the Painlevé II equation [14] with its related Toda system [15] for its non-commutative analogs and to derive the exact solutions of the generalized coupled dispersionless integrable system[16]. In section 22, we construct one-fold, two-fold and three-fold Darboux solutions of equation (1) with the help of linear representation for its coupling field variable uu and vv and then we generalise its NN-fold Darboux solutions in determinantal form as in terms of Wronskians.

Subsequently, we derive exact multi-solitonic solutions in the background of zero seed solutions for both coupling field variables uu and qq with graphical presentations of variety of solutions scattering elastically. This work also encloses the derivation of matrix zero curvature representation of CNW equation (1) possessing traceless matrices through its existed scalar Lax pair. That representation may be assumed to fit in the AKNS scheme [17] as it usually involves the parametric traceless matrices of order NN containing field variables. In last section we derive equation of continuity through the linear representation of CNW equation (1). We also calculate its several conserved densities with the help of its Riccati equation.

2 Linear representations and The Darboux solutions

This section encloses the Lax representation of Ito type coupled KdV equation which also called Integrable coupled nonlinear wave (CNW) equation (1) and the derivation of its equivalent zero-curvature from scalar Lax pair. Then by using the Darbaoux transformation [9, 10] on arbitrary function we construct the one-fold, two-fold and three-fold Darboux solutions to coupling field variables uu and vv in terms of seed solutions. Subsequently we generalize their NN-fold Darboux solutions in determinantal form.

2.1 Lax Pair and Zero-curvature representation

The coupled nonlinear wave equation (1) possesses is integrable [18, 19] and arises as the compatibility of subsequent linear system

ψx​x=(λ−u−β​q)​ψ.\psi_{xx}=\left(\lambda-u-\beta q\right)\psi.\\ (2)
ψt=(4​λ+2​u)​ψx−ux​ψ.\psi_{t}=\left(4\lambda+2u\right)\psi_{x}-u_{x}\psi. (3)

where q=v2q=v^{2} , β=14​λ\beta=\frac{1}{4\lambda} and λ\lambda is spectral parameter. It is easy to obtain CNW equation (1) by elimination of arbitrary function ψx​x\psi_{xx} from above linear system.

Proposition 2.1

By introducing a column vector in terms of arbitrary function as F=(f0,f1)T=(ψ,ψx)TF=(f_{0},f_{1})^{T}=(\psi,\psi_{x})^{T}, we may construct the matrix zero-curvature representation of CNW equation (1).

Proof

Consider the following linear system for arbitrary function FF

{∂xF=A​F∂tF=B​F,\left\{\begin{array}[]{lr}\partial_{x}F=AF\\ \partial_{t}F=BF\end{array}\right., (4)

where AA and BB are the matrices of order 22 to be determined, the compatibility of linear system (4) yields zero-curvature form as below

∂tA−∂xB+[A,B]=0,\partial_{t}A-\partial_{x}B+[A,B]=0, (5)

This can be shown that with the help of F=(f0,f1)T=(ψ,ψx)TF=(f_{0},f_{1})^{T}=(\psi,\psi_{x})^{T}, the eigenvalue equation L​ψ=λ​ψL\psi=\lambda\psi will take the following form

∂x(f0,f1)T=A​(f0,f1)T,\displaystyle\partial_{x}(f_{0},f_{1})^{T}=A(f_{0},f_{1})^{T}, (6)

where A=[01λ−u−β​q0]A=\begin{bmatrix}0&1\\ \lambda-u-\beta q&0\end{bmatrix} and can also be written as Fx=A​FF_{x}=AF. For the temporal part, let take the derivatiion of ψt=(4​λ+2​u)​ψx−ux​ψ\psi_{t}=\left(4\lambda+2u\right)\psi_{x}-u_{x}\psi with respect to xx, then by using ψx​x=(λ−u−β​q)​ψ\psi_{xx}=\left(\lambda-u-\beta q\right)\psi in resulting expression , we get

ψt​x=ux​ψx+4​λ2​ψ−2​λ​u​ψ−v2​ψ−2​u2​ψ−u​v2​ψ2​λ−ux​x​ψ,\psi_{tx}=u_{x}\psi_{x}+4\lambda^{2}\psi-2\lambda u\psi-v^{2}\psi-2u^{2}\psi-\frac{uv^{2}\psi}{2\lambda}-u_{xx}\psi, (7)

Now combining equation (3) and above equation, we obtain Ft=B​FF_{t}=BF, where

B=[−ux4​λ+2​u4​λ2−2​λ​u−v2−2​u2−u​v22​λ−ux​xux],B=\begin{bmatrix}-u_{x}&4\lambda+2u\\ 4\lambda^{2}-2\lambda u-v^{2}-2u^{2}-\frac{uv^{2}}{2\lambda}-u_{xx}&u_{x}\end{bmatrix}, (8)

Remark

The above matrix zero-curvature representation is derived from its scalar analogue presented in [18] whose compatibility condition is equivalent to ito type system as CNW equation (1) and the method mentioned above is straight forward to calculate the matrix zero curvatue representation from existed scalar Lax pair.

2.2 Darboux solutions

Here we construct the explicit Darboux expressions for the field variables uu and vv which connect the old solutions of CNW equation (1) to its new solutions through the particular solutions of linear equations (2) and (3). In order to construct the Darboux solutions for the coupled field variables uu and vv, let u⁡[1]u[1] and q⁡[1]q[1] are new solutions of CNW equation (1) and ψ⁡[1]\psi[1] is also a new solution of its associated linear system, then linear equation (2) with these new solution becomes

ψx​x​[1]=(λ−u⁡[1]−β​q​[1])​ψ​[1],\psi_{xx}[1]=\left(\lambda-u[1]-\beta q[1]\right)\psi[1], (9)

the transformation on arbitrary function is defined as

ψ⁡[1]=ψx−σ1​ψ,\psi[1]=\psi_{x}-\sigma_{1}\psi, (10)

where σ1=ψ1​xψ1\sigma_{1}=\frac{\psi_{1x}}{\psi_{1}} and the ψ1\psi_{1} is a particular solution can be calculated at λ=λ1​x\lambda=\lambda_{1x} from linear system (2) and (3) with provided seed solutions. Now substitute the value of ψ⁡[1]\psi[1] from equation (10) into transformed expression (9) then by using the original linear system (2), we can extract one step Darboux transformation on uu and qq as below

u⁡[1]=u+2​σ1​x,u[1]=u+2\sigma_{1x}, (11)
q⁡[1]=q−qx​σ1−1,q[1]=q-q_{x}\sigma_{1}^{-1}, (12)

respectively. In above transformations u⁡[1]u[1] and q⁡[1]q[1] are the new solutions generated from old solutions uu and qq through the particular solutions of linear system (2) and (3). This can be shown that with trivial solutions u=0u=0, q=0q=0, there is no variation on q⁡[1]q[1] that remains trivial and this problem can be eliminated by substituting the value of qxq_{x} from first equation of system (1), then finally we can express transformation (22) in following form

q⁡[1]=q−K​d​V​(u)​σ1−1,q[1]=q-KdV(u)\sigma_{1}^{-1}, (13)

where K​d​V​(u)=ut−ux​x​x−6​u​uxKdV(u)=u_{t}-u_{xxx}-6uu_{x} which generates non-trivial solutions for q⁡[2]q[2], q⁡[3]q[3], …, and so on.

Remark

For particular case, taking coupling field variable vv as constant the Darboux transformation (11) of KdV equation for fixed seed solution yields its real valued rational solutions as discussed in [20] for real parametric particular solutions and this transformation can also be applied to generate its special class of solutions as positon solutions for periodic generating function σ\sigma. Here our focus is to discuss only about multi-solitonic solutions CNW (1) with their conserved densities therefore we omit here to incorporate the non-solitonic behaviours.

2.3 Two and Three Fold Darboux transformations

The two-fold Darboux transformation for arbitrary fuction ψ\psi can be written as

ψ⁡[2]=(dd​x−ψ2​x​[1]ψ2​[1])​(dd​x−ψ1​xψ1)​ψ,\psi[2]=\left(\frac{d}{dx}-\frac{\psi_{2x}[1]}{\psi_{2}[1]}\right)\left(\frac{d}{dx}-\frac{\psi_{1x}}{\psi_{1}}\right)\psi, (14)

and ψ2​[1]\psi_{2}[1] can be calculated from following expression

ψ2​[1]=ψ2​x−ψ1​xψ1​ψ2,\psi_{2}[1]=\psi_{2x}-\frac{\psi_{1x}}{\psi_{1}}\psi_{2}, (15)

where ψ2\psi_{2} is the particular solution linear systems (2) and (3) at λ=λ2\lambda=\lambda_{2}, simply we can write two-fold transformation (14) as ratio of Wronskians

ψ⁡[2]=W⁡(ψ1,ψ2,ψ)W⁡(ψ1,ψ2).\psi[2]=\frac{W(\psi_{1},\psi_{2},\psi)}{W(\psi_{1},\psi_{2})}. (16)
W⁡(ψ1,ψ2,ψ)=|ψ1ψ2ψψ1(1)ψ2(1)ψ(1)ψ1(2)ψ2(2)ψ(2)|,W⁡(ψ1,ψ2)=|ψ1ψ2ψ1(1)ψ2(1)|W(\psi_{1},\psi_{2},\psi)=\begin{vmatrix}\psi_{1}&\psi_{2}&\psi\\ \psi_{1}^{(1)}&\psi_{2}^{(1)}&\psi^{(1)}\\ \psi_{1}^{(2)}&\psi_{2}^{(2)}&\psi^{(2)}\\ \end{vmatrix},W(\psi_{1},\psi_{2})=\begin{vmatrix}\psi_{1}&\psi_{2}\\ \psi_{1}^{(1)}&\psi_{2}^{(1)}\\ \end{vmatrix} (17)

here the superscripts (i)(i) represent the order of derivatives. Similarly, we can construct the ψ⁡[3]=(dd​x−ψ3​x​[2]ψ3​[2])​ψ​[2]\psi[3]=\left(\frac{d}{dx}-\frac{\psi_{3x}[2]}{\psi_{3}[2]}\right)\psi[2] in terms of Wronskians as below

ψ⁡[3]=W⁡(ψ1,ψ2,ψ3,ψ)W⁡(ψ1,ψ2,ψ3),\psi[3]=\frac{W(\psi_{1},\psi_{2},\psi_{3},\psi)}{W(\psi_{1},\psi_{2},\psi_{3})}, (18)

where

W⁡(ψ1,ψ2,ψ3,ψ)=|ψ1ψ2ψ3ψψ1(1)ψ2(1)ψ3(1)ψ(1)ψ1(2)ψ2(2)ψ3(2)ψ(2)ψ1(3)ψ2(3)ψ3(3)ψ(3)|W(\psi_{1},\psi_{2},\psi_{3},\psi)=\begin{vmatrix}\psi_{1}&\psi_{2}&\psi_{3}&\psi\\ \psi_{1}^{(1)}&\psi_{2}^{(1)}&\psi_{3}^{(1)}&\psi^{(1)}\\ \psi_{1}^{(2)}&\psi_{2}^{(2)}&\psi_{3}^{(2)}&\psi^{(2)}\\ \psi_{1}^{(3)}&\psi_{2}^{(3)}&\psi_{3}^{(3)}&\psi^{(3)}\\ \end{vmatrix} (19)
W⁡(ψ1,ψ2,ψ3)=|ψ1ψ2ψ3ψ1(1)ψ2(1)ψ3(1)ψ1(2)ψ2(2)ψ3(2)ψ1(3)ψ2(3)ψ3(3)|.W(\psi_{1},\psi_{2},\psi_{3})=\begin{vmatrix}\psi_{1}&\psi_{2}&\psi_{3}\\ \psi_{1}^{(1)}&\psi_{2}^{(1)}&\psi_{3}^{(1)}\\ \psi_{1}^{(2)}&\psi_{2}^{(2)}&\psi_{3}^{(2)}\\ \psi_{1}^{(3)}&\psi_{2}^{(3)}&\psi_{3}^{(3)}\\ \end{vmatrix}. (20)

Here we have presented Darboux transformations for arbitrary function ψ\psi upto three-fold in terms of Wronskians. In following proposition 2.2, we elaborate a procedure [9, 21] to generalise the NN-fold transformation for the coupling field variables uu and qq in compact form as the logarithmic derivative of Wronskians.

Proposition 2.2

With the help of one-fold Darboux transformations, we can construct NN-fold Darboux transformations for coupling field variables in following compact forms

u⁡[N]=u−2​η1​x,u[N]=u-2\eta_{1x}, (21)

and

q⁡[N]=q−qx​η1−1,q[N]=q-q_{x}\eta_{1}^{-1}, (22)

here η1=dd​x​log⁡W⁡(ψ1,ψ2,…,ψN)\eta_{1}=\frac{d}{dx}\log{W\left(\psi_{1},\psi_{2},...,\psi_{N}\right)} and W⁡(ψ1,ψ2,…​…,ψN)W(\psi_{1},\psi_{2},......,\psi_{N}) is Wronskian of order NN.
Proof:
The second iteration of (10) yields two-fold Darboux transformation on ψ\psi

ψ⁡[2]=(dd​x−σ2)​ψ​[1]=(dd​x−σ2)​(dd​x−σ1)​ψ\psi[2]=\left(\frac{d}{dx}-\sigma_{2}\right)\psi[1]=\left(\frac{d}{dx}-\sigma_{2}\right)\left(\frac{d}{dx}-\sigma_{1}\right)\psi (23)

with σ2=ψ2′​[1]​ψ2−1​[1]\sigma_{2}=\psi_{2}^{\prime}[1]\psi_{2}^{-1}[1] and ψ2​[1]\psi_{2}[1] can be calculated as ψ2​[1]=(dd​x−σ1)​ψ2\psi_{2}[1]=\left(\frac{d}{dx}-\sigma_{1}\right)\psi_{2}, here ψ2\psi_{2} is the particular solution of linear systems (2) and (3) at λ=λ2\lambda=\lambda_{2}. Similarly the two-fold Darboux transformation on uu and qq respectively can be written as

u⁡[2]=u+2​σ1​x+2​σ2​xu[2]=u+2\sigma_{1x}+2\sigma_{2x} (24)
q⁡[2]=q−K​d​V​(u)​σ1−1−K​d​V​(u⁡[1])​σ2−1.q[2]=q-KdV(u)\sigma_{1}^{-1}-KdV(u[1])\sigma_{2}^{-1}. (25)

After NN iteration we obtain the NN-fold Darboux transformations as below

ψ⁡[N]=(dd​x−σN)​(dd​x−σN−1)​(dd​x−σN−2)​…​(dd​x−σ2)​(dd​x−σ1)​ψ\psi[N]=\left(\frac{d}{dx}-\sigma_{N}\right)\left(\frac{d}{dx}-\sigma_{N-1}\right)\left(\frac{d}{dx}-\sigma_{N-2}\right)...\left(\frac{d}{dx}-\sigma_{2}\right)\left(\frac{d}{dx}-\sigma_{1}\right)\psi (26)
u⁡[N]=u+2​∑i=1Nσi′.u[N]=u+2\sum_{i=1}^{N}\sigma^{\prime}_{i}. (27)
q⁡[N]=q−∑i=1NK​d​V​(u⁡[i−1])​σi−1.q[N]=q-\sum_{i=1}^{N}KdV(u[i-1])\sigma_{i}^{-1}. (28)

with σi=ψi′​[i−1]​ψi−1​[i−1]\sigma_{i}=\psi^{\prime}_{i}[i-1]\psi^{-1}_{i}[i-1]. Now in order construct NN-fold Darboux transformations in terms of Wronskian, we start with NN-fold Darboux transformation for arbitrary function ψ\psi in following form

ψ⁡[N]=D⁡[N]​ψ=ψ(N)+η1​ψ(N−1)+η2​ψ(N−2)+…..+ηN−1​ψ(1)+ηN​ψ.\psi[N]=D[N]\psi=\psi^{(N)}+\eta_{1}\psi^{(N-1)}+\eta_{2}\psi^{(N-2)}+.....+\eta_{N-1}\psi^{(1)}+\eta_{N}\psi. (29)

which is an equivalent representation of (26), now we can easily show that the linear system (11) under the NN-fold transformation (29)(\ref{NFS}) may lead the following transformations

u⁡[N]=u−η1​x,q⁡[N]=q−qx​η1−1.u[N]=u-\eta_{1x},q[N]=q-q_{x}\eta_{1}^{-1}. (30)

The coefficient η1\eta_{1} in NN-th order linear differential operator D⁡[N]D[N] can be determine from the following system of NN linear algebraic equations

∑i=1Nηi​ψN−i=−ψiN\sum_{i=1}^{N}\eta_{i}\psi^{N-i}=-\psi^{N}_{i} (31)

where i=1,2,3,…​…,Ni=1,2,3,......,N that which can be derived by taking ψ=ψi\psi=\psi_{i} as ii-th particular solution into the equivalent form of NN-fold Darboux representation of (29), we can calculate the η1\eta_{1} in following form by applying the Kramer rule from above system (31)

η1=−|ψ1ψ1′⋯ψ1N−1ψNN⋱ψnψN′⋯ψNN−1ψNN|W(ψ1,ψ2,…..,ψN)=dd​x​log⁡W⁡(ψ1,ψ2,…,ψN).\eta_{1}=-\frac{\begin{vmatrix}\psi_{1}&\psi^{\prime}_{1}&\cdots&\psi^{N-1}_{1}&\psi^{N}_{N}\\ \vdots&\vdots&\ddots&\vdots&\vdots\\ \psi_{n}&\psi^{\prime}_{N}&\cdots&\psi^{N-1}_{N}&\psi^{N}_{N}\end{vmatrix}}{W\left(\psi_{1},\psi_{2},.....,\psi_{N}\right)}=\frac{d}{dx}\log{W\left(\psi_{1},\psi_{2},...,\psi_{N}\right)}. (32)

Now we can express NN-fold transformation (30) in terms of Wronskian as below

u⁡[N]=u−d2d​x2​log⁡W⁡(ψ1,ψ2,…,ψN).u[N]=u-\frac{d^{2}}{dx^{2}}\log{W\left(\psi_{1},\psi_{2},...,\psi_{N}\right)}. (33)

Now with the help of two-fold and three-fold transformations ψ⁡[2]\psi[2], ψ⁡[3]\psi[3], we can directly generalise the NN-fold expression for arbitrary function ψ\psi in terms of ratio of Wronskians as below

ψ⁡[N]=W⁡(ψ1,ψ2,…​…,ψN,ψ)W⁡(ψ1,ψ2,…​…,ψN),\psi[N]=\frac{W(\psi_{1},\psi_{2},......,\psi_{N},\psi)}{W(\psi_{1},\psi_{2},......,\psi_{N})}, (34)

here

W(ψ1,ψ2,….ψN)=|ψ1ψ2⋯ψNψ1(1)ψ2(1)⋯ψN(1)⋱ψ1(n−1)ψ2(n−1)⋯ψN(n−1)|,W(\psi_{1},\psi_{2},....\psi_{N})=\begin{vmatrix}\psi_{1}&\psi_{2}&\cdots&\psi_{N}\\ \psi_{1}^{(1)}&\psi_{2}^{(1)}&\cdots&\psi_{N}^{(1)}\\ \vdots&\vdots&\ddots&\vdots\\ \psi_{1}^{(n-1)}&\psi_{2}^{(n-1)}&\cdots&\psi_{N}^{(n-1)}\end{vmatrix}, (35)

and

W(ψ1,ψ2,….ψN,ψ)=|ψ1ψ2⋯ψNψψ1(1)ψ2(1)⋯ψN(1)ψ(1)⋱ψ1(n−1)ψ2(n−1)⋯ψN(n−1)ψ(n−1)|,W(\psi_{1},\psi_{2},....\psi_{N},\psi)=\begin{vmatrix}\psi_{1}&\psi_{2}&\cdots&\psi_{N}&\psi\\ \psi_{1}^{(1)}&\psi_{2}^{(1)}&\cdots&\psi_{N}^{(1)}&\psi^{(1)}\\ \vdots&\vdots&\ddots&\vdots&\vdots\\ \psi_{1}^{(n-1)}&\psi_{2}^{(n-1)}&\cdots&\psi_{N}^{(n-1)}&\psi^{(n-1)}\end{vmatrix}, (36)

in above determinants ψj(i)\psi_{j}^{(i)} stands for ii-th derivative of ψj\psi_{j} with respect to xx as ψj(i)=di​ψjd​xi\psi_{j}^{(i)}=\frac{d^{i}\psi_{j}}{dx^{i}}. In subsequent section, we derive up to three soliton solutions for the coupling filed variables uu and vv in the background of zero seed solutions with their graphical representations.

3 Exact solitonic solutions

This section encloses the derivation of exact solutions to the CNW equation (1) as one -soliton, two-soliton and three-soliton solutions for field variables uu and vv through help of their Darboux transformations in background of zero seed solutions. In order to construct non-trivial exact solitonic solutions for field variable vv, we apply the NN time iterative form (28) for qq embedded with KdV equation.

3.1 One-soliton solutions

Let us start with simplest trivial solutions of CNW (1) as u=0u=0 and v=0v=0 also q=0q=0, then one-fold Darboux for uu will take the following form

u⁡[1]=2​dd​x​ψ1​xψ1=2​d2d​x2​log⁡ψ1,u[1]=2\frac{d}{dx}\frac{\psi_{1x}}{\psi_{1}}=2\frac{d^{2}}{dx^{2}}\log\psi_{1}, (37)

the particular solution ψ1\psi_{1} can be calculated from linear system (2) at λ=λ1\lambda=\lambda_{1} as below

ψ1​(x,t)=2​cosh⁡(k1​x+4​k1​λ1​t),\psi_{1}(x,t)=2\cosh{(k_{1}x+4k_{1}\lambda_{1}t)}, (38)

Now after substituting the above value in expression (37) and after some simplification we get one-soliton solution

u⁡[1]=2​k12​sech2⁡(k1​x+4​k1​λ1​t),u[1]=2k_{1}^{2}\sech^{2}{(k_{1}x+4k_{1}\lambda_{1}t)}, (39)

3.2 Two-soliton solution u⁡[2]u[2]

Now the two-fold Darboux transformation with trivial solution u=0 will take the following form

u⁡[2]=2​d2d​x2​log⁡[W⁡(ψ1,ψ2)],u[2]=2\frac{d^{2}}{dx^{2}}\log{[W(\psi_{1},\psi_{2})}], (40)

where

u⁡[2]=2​d2d​x2​log⁡|ψ1ψ2d​ψ1d​xd​ψ2d​x|,u[2]=2\frac{d^{2}}{dx^{2}}\log\begin{vmatrix}\psi_{1}&\psi_{2}\\ \frac{d\psi_{1}}{dx}&\frac{d\psi_{2}}{dx}\end{vmatrix}, (41)

We can calculate the value for ψ1\psi_{1} and ψ2\psi_{2} from the linear system (2) at λ=λ1\lambda=\lambda_{1} and λ=λ2\lambda=\lambda_{2} respectively as below

ψ1​(x,t)=2​cosh⁡(k1​x+4​k1​λ1​t),\psi_{1}(x,t)=2\cosh{(k_{1}x+4k_{1}\lambda_{1}t)}, (42)
ψ2​(x,t)=2​sinh⁡(k2​x+4​k2​λ2​t),\psi_{2}(x,t)=2\sinh{(k_{2}x+4k_{2}\lambda_{2}t)}, (43)

After substituting above values into equation (41), we get following results

u⁡[2]=2​d2d​x2​log⁡|2​cosh⁡(k1​x+4​k1​λ1​t)2​sinh⁡(k2​x+4​k2​λ2​t)2​k1​sinh⁡(k1​x+4​k1​λ1​t)2​k2​cosh⁡(k2​x+4​k2​λ2​t)|,u[2]=2\frac{d^{2}}{dx^{2}}\log\begin{vmatrix}2\cosh(k_{1}x+4k_{1}\lambda_{1}t)&2\sinh(k_{2}x+4k_{2}\lambda_{2}t)\\ 2k_{1}\sinh(k_{1}x+4k_{1}\lambda_{1}t)&2k_{2}\cosh(k_{2}x+4k_{2}\lambda_{2}t)\end{vmatrix}, (44)

now expanding the determinate and taking derivations, finally we obtain the following result

u⁡[2]=4​(k22−k12)​[k22​cosh⁡(2​γ1)+k12​cosh⁡(2​γ2)+k22−k12((k2−k1)​cosh⁡(γ1+γ2)+(k2+k1)​cosh⁡(γ1−γ2))2],u[2]=4(k_{2}^{2}-k_{1}^{2})\left[\frac{k_{2}^{2}\cosh(2\gamma_{1})+k_{1}^{2}\cosh(2\gamma_{2})+k_{2}^{2}-k_{1}^{2}}{((k_{2}-k_{1})\cosh{(\gamma_{1}+\gamma_{2})}+(k_{2}+k_{1})\cosh{(\gamma_{1}-\gamma_{2})})^{2}}\right], (45)

which is two-soliton solution well know for KdV equation because KdV equation is embedded as essential part in CNW equation (1) where γ1=k1​x+4​k1​λ1​t\gamma_{1}=k_{1}x+4k_{1}\lambda_{1}t and γ2=k2​x+4​k2​λ2​t\gamma_{2}=k_{2}x+4k_{2}\lambda_{2}t. The inelastic scattering of the two solitons has been visualised in one dimension as well as on plane as below

3.3 Two-soliton solution q⁡[2]q[2] for coupling variable vv

In this part of section 22, we derive two-soliton solution to coupling field variable vv, as it is obvious from NN-the expression () at N=1N=1, q⁡[1]=0q[1]=0 implies v⁡[1]=0v[1]=0, it means at first iteration only KdV solution appears. But the second iteration at N=2N=2 yields non zero two soliton solution to coupling field variable vv as below

q⁡[2]=q⁡[1]−(u​[1]t−u​[1]x​x​x−6​u​[1]​u​[1]x)​σ2​[1]−1,q[2]=q[1]-\left(u[1]_{t}-u[1]_{xxx}-6u[1]u[1]_{x}\right)\sigma_{2}[1]^{-1}, (46)

Now substitute the calculated values of u⁡[1]u[1] and σ2​[1]\sigma_{2}[1] in last express (46) and then after simplification, we get

q⁡[2]=[16k13(k12−λ)sechγ12tanhγ1(k2cothγ2−k1tanhγ1)](k12−k22),q[2]=\frac{\left[16k_{1}^{3}(k_{1}^{2}-\lambda)\sech{\gamma_{1}}^{2}\tanh{\gamma_{1}}(k_{2}\coth{\gamma_{2}}-k_{1}\tanh{\gamma_{1}})\right]}{(k_{1}^{2}-k_{2}^{2})}, (47)

this straight forward to obtain v⁡[2]v[2] by taking square root of q⁡[2]q[2] which is again two-soliton solution. The elastic interaction of these two solitons has been show in one dimension.

Here we have calculated two-soliton solutions for the coupling field variables uu and vv which simultaneously satisfy CNW equation (1). The two-soliton solution u⁡[2]u[2] can be assumed as interaction of KdV solitons associated to CNW equation (1), where as v⁡[2]v[2] which can be obtained from q⁡[2]q[2] also two-soliton solution differs from u⁡[2]u[2] associated to same equation (1) that composed by soliton and anti-soliton propagating in opposite directions and interact elastically.

3.4 Three-soliton solution u⁡[3]u[3]

The three-fold Darboux transformation (21) with trivial solution u=0 will take the following form

u⁡[3]=2​d2d​x2​log⁡[W⁡(ψ1,ψ2,ψ3)],u[3]=2\frac{d^{2}}{dx^{2}}\log\left[W(\psi_{1},\psi_{2},\psi_{3})\right], (48)

we can compute the value for ψ3\psi_{3} form the linear system (2) at λ=λ3\lambda=\lambda_{3} which is given by

ψ3​(x,t)=2​cosh⁡(γ3).\psi_{3}(x,t)=2\cosh{(\gamma_{3})}. (49)

with

γ3=k3​x+4​k3​λ3​t.\gamma_{3}=k_{3}x+4k_{3}\lambda_{3}t. (50)

Now after substituting these values in equation (48) and simplifying, we get

u[3]=[−(k1k3(−k12+k32)sinhγ1sinhγ2sinhγ3+k2coshγ2(k1(k12−k22)coshγ3sinhγ1+k3(k22−k32)coshγ1sinhγ3))2+(k1(−k22+k32)coshγ3sinhγ1sinhγ2+coshγ1(k2(k12−k32)coshγ2coshγ3+(−k12+k22)k3sinhγ2sinhγ3))(k1(k12−k22−k32)(k22−k32)coshγ3sinhγ1sinhγ2+coshγ1(−k2(k12−k32)(−k12+k22−k32)coshγ2coshγ3−(k12−k22)k3(k12+k22−k32)sinhγ2sinhγ3))]/[k1(−k22+k32)coshγ3sinhγ1sinhγ2+coshγ1(k2(k12−k32)coshγ2coshγ3+k3(−k12+k22)sinhγ2sinhγ3)]2,u[3]=[-(k_{1}k_{3}(-k_{1}^{2}+k_{3}^{2})\sinh{\gamma_{1}}\sinh{\gamma_{2}}\sinh{\gamma_{3}}+k2\cosh{\gamma_{2}}(k1(k1^{2}-k2^{2})\cosh{\gamma_{3}}\\ \sinh{\gamma_{1}}+k3(k2^{2}-k3^{2})\cosh{\gamma_{1}}\sinh{\gamma_{3}}))^{2}+(k1(-k2^{2}+k3^{2})\cosh{\gamma_{3}}\sinh{\gamma_{1}}\sinh{\gamma_{2}}\\ +\cosh{\gamma_{1}}(k2(k1^{2}-k3^{2})\cosh{\gamma_{2}}\cosh{\gamma_{3}}+(-k1^{2}+k2^{2})k3\sinh{\gamma_{2}}\sinh{\gamma_{3}}))\\ (k1(k1^{2}-k2^{2}-k3^{2})(k2^{2}-k3^{2})\cosh{\gamma_{3}}\sinh{\gamma_{1}}\sinh{\gamma_{2}}+\cosh{\gamma_{1}}(-k2(k1^{2}-k3^{2})\\ (-k1^{2}+k2^{2}-k3^{2})\cosh{\gamma_{2}}\cosh{\gamma_{3}}-(k1^{2}-k2^{2})k3(k1^{2}+k2^{2}-k3^{2})\sinh{\gamma_{2}}\sinh{\gamma_{3}}))]\\ /[k_{1}(-k_{2}^{2}+k_{3}^{2})\cosh{\gamma_{3}}\sinh{\gamma_{1}}\sinh{\gamma_{2}}+\cosh{\gamma_{1}}\\ (k_{2}(k_{1}^{2}-k_{3}^{2})\cosh{\gamma_{2}}\cosh{\gamma_{3}}+k_{3}(-k_{1}^{2}+k_{2}^{2})\sinh{\gamma_{2}}\sinh{\gamma_{3}})]^{2}, (51)

which is the explicit expression of three-soliton solution for uu associated with CNW equation and the interactions of these solitons have been shown below.

4 Equation of Continuity and conserved densities

This section is devoted to construct the equation of continuity which is associated with CNW equation (1) and derivation of conserved densities incorporating its riccati equation.
For this purpose, let define a quantity Γ\Gamma in terms of arbitrary function, as below

Γ=ψ′ψ=(l​n​ψ)x,\Gamma=\frac{\psi^{\prime}}{\psi}=(ln\psi)_{x}, (56)

Now take the time derivative of Γ\Gamma and then make use of equation (3) in resulting expression, we get folowing result after simplification

∂Γ∂t=2​u′​Γ+(4​λ+2​u)​(ψ′′ψ−ψ′2ψ2)−u′′,\frac{\partial\Gamma}{\partial t}=2u^{\prime}\Gamma+\left(4\lambda+2u\right)\left(\frac{\psi^{\prime\prime}}{\psi}-\frac{{\psi^{\prime}}^{2}}{\psi^{2}}\right)-u^{\prime\prime}, (57)

and the space derivative of equation(56) can be written as

∂Γ∂x=ψ′′ψ−ψ′2ψ2,\frac{\partial\Gamma}{\partial x}=\frac{\psi^{\prime\prime}}{\psi}-\frac{{\psi^{\prime}}^{2}}{\psi^{2}}, (58)

Now eliminating (ψ′′ψ−ψ′2ψ2)\left(\frac{\psi^{\prime\prime}}{\psi}-\frac{{\psi^{\prime}}^{2}}{\psi^{2}}\right) from equation (57), and by using last equation equation(58), after simplification we obtain resulting expression as below

∂Γ∂t=∂∂x​[(4​λ+2​u)​Γ−u′],\frac{\partial\Gamma}{\partial t}=\frac{\partial}{\partial x}\left[(4\lambda+2u)\Gamma-u^{\prime}\right], (59)

or

∂ρ∂t−∂J∂x=0\frac{\partial\rho}{\partial t}-\frac{\partial J}{\partial x}=0 (60)

the above is the equation of continuity associated with CNW equation (1) involving density as ρ\rho and corresponding current as jj given as

J=(4​λ+2​u)​Γ−u′.J=(4\lambda+2u)\Gamma-u^{\prime}. (61)

We may construct the hierarchy of conserved densities for CNW equation (1) with the help of its riccati equation as calculated below.
It is straight forward to construct the riccati equation from expression (58) by using equation (2) as in the following form

∂Γ∂x+(u−λ+q4​λ)+Γ2=0,\frac{\partial\Gamma}{\partial x}+\left(u-\lambda+\frac{q}{4\lambda}\right)+\Gamma^{2}=0, (62)

Now by taking the derivation of above Riccati equation with respect xx, we obtain second order ordinary differential equation as

∂2Γ∂x2−2​Γ3+2​Γ​(λ−u−q4​λ)+u′+q′4​λ=0.\frac{\partial^{2}\Gamma}{\partial x^{2}}-2\Gamma^{3}+2\Gamma\left(\lambda-u-\frac{q}{4\lambda}\right)+u^{\prime}+\frac{q^{\prime}}{4\lambda}=0. (63)

Let consider following ansatz as the solution of above equation

Γ=∑n=1∞Γn​λ−n,\Gamma=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\Gamma_{n}\lambda^{-n}, (64)

where the quantities Γn\Gamma_{n} are to be determined which represent the densities associated with Ito type coupled equation (1). After substituting ansatz (64) into equation(63) and then expanding summation, finally the coefficients of λ0\lambda^{0}, λ−1\lambda^{-1} , λ−2\lambda^{-2} in resulting expression produce first three densities

Γ1=−u′2,\Gamma_{1}=-\frac{u^{\prime}}{2}, (65)
Γ2=u′′′4−q′8−12​u​u′,\Gamma_{2}=\frac{u^{\prime\prime\prime}}{4}-\frac{q^{\prime}}{8}-\frac{1}{2}uu^{\prime}, (66)
Γ3=u​Γ2+q4​Γ1−12​∂2∂x2​Γ2.\Gamma_{3}=u\Gamma_{2}+\frac{q}{4}\Gamma_{1}-\frac{1}{2}\frac{\partial^{2}}{\partial x^{2}}\Gamma_{2}. (67)

and the coefficients of NN-the terms yield the following relation

Γn+1=12​[2​u​Γn+q2​Γn−1+2​∑l=1m=n−2Γl​(∑k=1j=m−l+1Γk​Γj−k+1)−∂2∂x2​Γn],\Gamma_{n+1}=\frac{1}{2}\left[2u\Gamma_{n}+\frac{q}{2}\Gamma_{n-1}+2\sum_{l=1}^{m=n-2}\Gamma_{l}\left(\sum_{k=1}^{j=m-l+1}\Gamma_{k}\Gamma_{j-k+1}\right)-\frac{\partial^{2}}{\partial x^{2}}\Gamma_{n}\right], (68)

which holds for n=3,4,5,…,n=3,4,5,..., and with the help of that expression we may calculate all remaining conserved densities. Now we can expression (58) can be written in nn-th form Jn=(4​λ+2​u)​Γn−u′J_{n}=(4\lambda+2u)\Gamma_{n}-u^{\prime}that yields the corresponding currents.

5 Conclusion

In this article, we have calculated multi-solitonic solutions for coupling field variables uu, qq associted with Ito type coupled KdV equation (1) in Darboux framework and then their NN-fold Darboux transformations generalised in terms of Wronkians. We also derived its equation of continuity with hierarchy of conserved densities. For motivation, It is quite interesting to construct its Hirota bilinear form with multi-solitoinc solutions and comparable to our results obtained here, that will be discussed in a separate paper. Further, it is straight forward to calculate its noncommutative analogue with NN-fold Darboux solutions in terms of quasideterminats which may coincide with our results under commutative limit.
